cited.text:
### 6.1 Day 1

1. Report to the reception of your base office at 9:30 am with your original ID and education documents.
2. Collect your laptop from the IT desk. It arrives encrypted (BitLocker on Windows, FileVault on macOS) and enrolled in device management.
3. Set your password (minimum 14 characters) and register MFA on the Nimbus Authenticator app. You cannot access email, Slack or the HRMS without MFA.

| Requirement       | Value                                                                                                                        |

questions.q: What is the response time for a SEV1 incident and who gets paged?
questions.answer: For a SEV1 incident, the response time is **15 minutes** [1][2]. According to the SEV1 Runbook, the **primary and secondary on-call, Incident Commander rota, CISO, and CTO** are paged [1]. The Incident Reporting Procedure lists the **incident commander, CISO, CTO, and Head of Infrastructure & SRE** as engaged [2]. Both documents note the CISO and CTO are paged automatically for every SEV1 [3].
questions.query: What is the response time for a SEV1 incident and who gets paged?

cited.title: SEV1 Incident Response Runbook
cited.text:
## 2. Severity levels

| Severity | Definition | Response time | Who is paged |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEV1 | Customer-wide outage, or data breach suspected | 15 min | Primary + secondary on-call, Incident Commander rota, CISO and CTO |
| SEV2 | Service degraded for many customers (slow, partial features down) | 30 min | Primary on-call, Engineering Manager |
| SEV3 | Single customer impacted | 4 h | Primary on-call (business hours escalation) |
| SEV4 | Minor issue, no customer impact | Next business day | Ticket only |

When in doubt, declare the higher severity. Downgrading later is free; a late SEV1 is not.

cited.title: Incident Reporting Procedure
cited.text:
## 5. Severity classification

The SOC or on-call incident commander assigns the severity. Severity can be raised or lowered as more is learnt.

| Severity   | Definition                                                                           | Response time     | Who is engaged                                                       |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| SEV1       | Customer-wide outage, or confirmed breach of Confidential/Restricted data            | 15 minutes        | Incident commander; CISO and CTO paged; Head of Infrastructure & SRE |
| SEV2       | Significant degradation affecting many customers, or a contained security compromise | 30 minutes        | Incident commander, service owner, SOC lead                          |
| SEV3       | Issue affecting a single customer or user, or a policy violation without data loss   | 4 hours           | Service team or SOC analyst                                          |
| SEV4       | Minor issue, no customer impact                                                      | Next business day | Owning team via ticket                                               |

Response time means the time within which a responder acknowledges and starts working, 24x7 for SEV1 and SEV2, and during business hours for SEV3 and SEV4.

cited.title: SEV1 Incident Response Runbook
cited.text:
## 3. Declare

Anyone can declare. In Slack:

```
/incident declare sev1 "NimbusOps UI and API returning 503 for all tenants"
```

This creates `#inc-<date>-<number>`, opens a Zoom bridge, starts the timeline and pages per the table above. The CISO (Sameer Khan) and CTO (Meera Iyer) are paged automatically for every SEV1.

questions.reference: SEV1 (customer-wide outage or confirmed breach of Confidential/Restricted data) needs a response within 15 minutes; the CISO and CTO are paged along with the incident commander.

NimbusOps commits to 99.9% monthly availability, an RPO of 15 minutes and an RTO of 1 hour. The primary region is AWS **ap-south-1 (Mumbai)** and the DR region is AWS **ap-south-2 (Hyderabad)**. All customer data must stay in India.

Today the DR region is a warm standby at about 30% capacity. Failover is a manual sequence of runbook steps (NIM/ENG/RB-001 Section 6), coordinated on a SEV1 bridge. Recent full drills:

| Drill | Measured RPO | Measured RTO | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 19 October 2025 | 9 min | 71 min | Fail (RTO) – DNS script needed a manual IAM fix |
| 18 April 2026 | 6 min | 47 min | Pass – MSK offset translation took 11 min |

We pass, but with little margin. The April drill needed 14 manual commands from 4 people, and the RTO depends on Karpenter being able to scale the DR cluster from 30% to full capacity during a regional event, when other AWS customers will be doing the same.

On 11 June 2026 the HarborTrack warehouse management system was unavailable for 2 hours 47 minutes after a Terraform change made during the wave 9 cutover removed database access for the application tier. cited.title: Al Noor Healthcare – Managed SOC Service Report
cited.text:
## 5. Notable incident - AN-SOC-0612 (P1)

- Date: 19 May 2026, detected 10:42 GST (12:12 IST).
- What happened: Phishing emails impersonating a supplier of imaging equipment were sent to 64 staff in procurement and radiology. Two users entered credentials on a fake login page; one account was used to create a mail-forwarding rule.
- Response: Accounts disabled and sessions revoked at 11:09 GST; malicious forwarding rule removed; 62 copies of the email purged from mailboxes; sender domain blocked. Containment completed at 11:23 GST (41 minutes after detection).
- Impact: No access to clinical systems or patient records, confirmed by review of Sentinel and EHR access logs. Al Noor's Data Protection Officer was informed and determined no regulatory notification was required.
- Follow-up: Conditional access policy now requires phishing-resistant MFA for procurement staff; targeted awareness session delivered on 2 June 2026.

questions.q: What counts as a SEV1 incident and how fast must on-call respond?
questions.answer: SEV1 covers a customer-wide outage, or a suspected data breach [1]; the Incident Reporting Procedure defines it as a customer-wide outage or a confirmed breach of Confidential/Restricted data [2]. On-call must acknowledge and start working within 15 minutes, 24x7 [1][2].

cited.title: SEV1 Incident Response Runbook
cited.text:
## 2. Severity levels

| Severity | Definition | Response time | Who is paged |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEV1 | Customer-wide outage, or data breach suspected | 15 min | Primary + secondary on-call, Incident Commander rota, CISO and CTO |
| SEV2 | Service degraded for many customers (slow, partial features down) | 30 min | Primary on-call, Engineering Manager |
| SEV3 | Single customer impacted | 4 h | Primary on-call (business hours escalation) |
| SEV4 | Minor issue, no customer impact | Next business day | Ticket only |

When in doubt, declare the higher severity. Downgrading later is free; a late SEV1 is not.

cited.title: Incident Reporting Procedure
cited.text:
## 5. Severity classification

The SOC or on-call incident commander assigns the severity. Severity can be raised or lowered as more is learnt.

| Severity   | Definition                                                                           | Response time     | Who is engaged                                                       |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| SEV1       | Customer-wide outage, or confirmed breach of Confidential/Restricted data            | 15 minutes        | Incident commander; CISO and CTO paged; Head of Infrastructure & SRE |
| SEV2       | Significant degradation affecting many customers, or a contained security compromise | 30 minutes        | Incident commander, service owner, SOC lead                          |
| SEV3       | Issue affecting a single customer or user, or a policy violation without data loss   | 4 hours           | Service team or SOC analyst                                          |
| SEV4       | Minor issue, no customer impact                                                      | Next business day | Owning team via ticket                                               |

Response time means the time within which a responder acknowledges and starts working, 24x7 for SEV1 and SEV2, and during business hours for SEV3 and SEV4.

### 8. Acceptance criteria

The inventory sync stream is accepted when all of the following are met in UAT and confirmed in the first 30 days of hypercare:

| **#**   | **Criterion**                                                                      | **Evidence**            |
|---------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| AC-1    | p95 stock refresh latency under 15 minutes over 7 consecutive days, all 480 stores | SAC latency report      |
| AC-2    | Peak test at 2x Diwali-day volume passed with no lost messages                     | SIT 2 test report       |
| AC-3    | Availability API p95 under 300 ms at 500 requests per second                       | Performance test report |
| AC-4    | Daily reconciliation differences above 0.5% in fewer than 5 stores per day         | Reconciliation report   |

All NimbusOps customer data is stored in India, in Amazon Web Services **ap-south-1 (Mumbai)**, with disaster recovery in **ap-south-2 (Hyderabad)**. We do not replicate customer data outside India.

cited.title: BRD – NimbusOps AI Alert Summaries
cited.text:
### 6. Data, security and compliance

- All processing stays in AWS **ap-south-1 (Mumbai)**, the NimbusOps primary region, with failover to ap-south-2 (Hyderabad). No alert data leaves India, in line with the NimbusOps data residency commitment.
- The language model runs inside the NimbusOps AWS account; customer data is **not used to train** any model and is not shared with third parties.
- Only alert metadata (rule name, host, service, metric value, timestamps) is sent to the model, never raw log lines.
- Summaries are stored with the incident and follow the same 13-month retention as events.
- The feature must pass a SOC 2 Type II control review before GA, as it adds a new processing component within the audit scope.
- Every summary is labelled "AI-generated" in the UI and notifications.

Personal data may be transferred outside India except to countries restricted by notification of the Central Government. NimbusOps customer data is hosted in India (AWS ap-south-1 Mumbai, DR in ap-south-2 Hyderabad). Transfers of employee data to the Dubai office are limited to what is needed for local HR administration.

cited.text:
## 5. Limitation of liability

- Liability cap: each party's total liability under the MSA in any contract year is limited to the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the event giving rise to the claim.
- Super-cap: for breaches of confidentiality or data protection obligations, the cap is two times (2x) the 12-month fees.
- Uncapped: fraud, wilful misconduct, gross negligence, and each party's indemnity for third-party intellectual property claims.
- Neither party is liable for indirect or consequential losses, including loss of profit, except under the uncapped items.

These caps are within the Nimbus standard position; any increase at renewal needs CFO and Legal approval, as set out in the Contract Review and Signing Authority Guideline and the Discount Approval Policy.

questions.q: How fast must a critical vulnerability on an internet-facing system be fixed?
questions.answer: A critical vulnerability on an internet-facing system must be fixed within 7 days [1]. If it is actively exploited, it must be fixed or mitigated within 72 hours on any system [1]. The deadline starts when the SOC raises the remediation ticket, which must happen within 1 business day of the scan result [1].
questions.query: How fast must a critical vulnerability on an internet-facing system be fixed?

cited.title: Vulnerability Management Standard
cited.text:
## 5. Severity and remediation deadlines

Severity is based on the CVSS v3.1 base score, raised by one level if the asset holds Restricted data or the vulnerability is listed as known-exploited.

| Severity (CVSS v3.1)   | Internet-facing systems   | Internal systems         |
|------------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------|
| Critical (9.0-10.0)    | 7 days                    | 15 days                  |
| High (7.0-8.9)         | 30 days                   | 45 days                  |
| Medium (4.0-6.9)       | 90 days                   | 120 days                 |
| Low (below 4.0)        | Next planned maintenance  | Next planned maintenance |

- Actively exploited Critical vulnerabilities (listed in the CISA KEV catalogue or flagged by CERT-In) must be fixed or mitigated within 72 hours, on any system. The CISO may order an emergency change outside the normal release window.
- The deadline starts when the SOC raises the remediation ticket, which must happen within 1 business day of the scan result.
- Endpoint operating system patches are pushed within 7 days of release; laptops that are not patched within 21 days lose network access until updated.

questions.reference: Within 7 days on internet-facing systems (15 days on internal systems); actively exploited Criticals within 72 hours.

questions.q: Who approves a risk exception for a Medium or Low vulnerability, and for how long?

cited.text:
## 6. Exceptions

If a vulnerability cannot be fixed by its deadline, the system owner raises a risk exception in the GRC tool before the deadline, with the reason, compensating controls (for example, a WAF rule or network isolation) and a target fix date.

| Severity     | Exception approved by                          | Maximum exception period   |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| Critical     | CISO and CTO jointly                           | 30 days                    |
| High         | CISO                                           | 90 days                    |
| Medium / Low | Engineering Manager with the Security Champion | 180 days                   |

Exceptions cannot be renewed more than once. An expired exception is treated as an overdue finding. Exceptions for client environments also need the written agreement of the client's security contact.

questions.doc: Privileged Access and Quarterly Access Review Procedure
questions.answer: Privileged access (which includes production access) is reviewed **every quarter** — the review windows open on 1 July, 1 October, 2 January and 1 April, with manager sign‑off due by the 15th (or 16th for the December quarter) [1].

cited.title: Privileged Access and Quarterly Access Review Procedure
cited.text:
### 6. Quarterly access review

All access to systems classified as Confidential or Restricted, and all privileged access, is reviewed **every quarter**.

| **Quarter ending**   | **Review window opens**   | **Manager sign-off due**   |
|----------------------|---------------------------|----------------------------|
| 30 June              | 1 July                    | 15 July                    |
| 30 September         | 1 October                 | 15 October                 |
| 31 December          | 2 January                 | 16 January                 |
| 31 March             | 1 April                   | 15 April                   |

Steps:

1.	The SOC exports user and role lists from each system into the access review tool on the first working day of the review window.

2.	Each line manager confirms ("keep") or removes ("revoke") every access of each team member within **10 business days**.

3.	System owners review privileged and service accounts for their system in the same window.

4.	Access not confirmed by the due date is **revoked automatically** on the next business day.

5.	The SOC records results and exceptions; the completion rate is reported to the CISO. The Information Security Policy target is 100% on time.

## 2. Do you hire freshers?

Yes. Freshers are hired at all three plants, at the R&D centre and in the field force.

questions.q: When are supplies stopped for overdue payments?
questions.answer: Supplies are stopped when any invoice is more than 15 days overdue (i.e. 45 days from invoice for a stockist on 30-day terms), until the overdue invoice is paid. cited.text:
## 7. Recalled products

7.1 When Sanjeevani recalls a batch, we publish the product, batch number and reason on our website and inform stockists, pharmacies and the drug regulators. Pharmacies must stop selling the batch immediately. 7.2 Refund: all recalled stock returned through the trade receives full credit at the invoice price plus the cost of return freight, whether the packs are sealed, opened or part-used. The 2% expiry cap does not apply to recalls. 7.3 Patients holding a recalled product may return it to the pharmacy where it was bought; the pharmacy gives a replacement pack of the same medicine (or a refund if no replacement is available) and is reimbursed by Sanjeevani through its stockist. 7.4 Example - batch CR-2309 (August 2025): Sanjeevani voluntarily recalled batch CR-2309 of Sanjeevani Cough Relief Syrup in August 2025 because of a label misprint (the label showed the wrong manufacturing licence number). There was no safety impact. 18,400 bottles had been distributed. Stockists and pharmacies received full credit at invoice price for every returned bottle, and freight was reimbursed.

### 1.1 What information should I give?

1. The name of the medicine (for example "Cardivas 10"), the batch number and expiry date printed on the strip, bottle or tube.

## 2. Exit loads

**What exit load applies to the equity funds?**

| Scheme | Exit load |
|---|---|
| Kaveri Bluechip Fund | 1% if redeemed within 365 days of allotment |
| Kaveri Flexi Cap Fund | 1% if redeemed within 365 days of allotment |
| Kaveri Small Cap Opportunities | 1% if redeemed within 365 days of allotment |
| Kaveri Short Duration Fund | Nil |
| Kaveri Arbitrage Fund | 0.25% if redeemed within 15 days of allotment |

**Is there an exit load if I redeem my Flexi Cap units after 8 months?**
Yes. Eight months is within 365 days of allotment, so an exit load of 1% applies to those units. Units held for more than 365 days carry no exit load.

**How is the exit load worked out if I invested through a SIP?**
Each SIP instalment is treated separately on a first-in, first-out basis. When you redeem, the oldest units are redeemed first, and only units still within 365 days of their own allotment date carry the 1% load.

**Does a switch between Kaveri funds attract exit load?**
Yes. A switch is treated as a redemption from the first scheme for exit load purposes.

**Are dividend reinvestment units charged exit load?**
No.

**What is the exit load on the PMS?**

| Withdrawal within (from date of each contribution) | Exit load |
|---|---|
| Year 1 | 3% |
| Year 2 | 2% |
| Year 3 | 1% |
| After 3 years | Nil |

**And on the AIF?**
The Kaveri Long-Short AIF III has a 12-month lock-in from each contribution. After the lock-in, an exit load of 1% applies in months 13–24 and nil after that. Redemptions are monthly with 30 days' notice.

### 6. Fee options

Clients choose one fee structure at onboarding. The structure may be changed once a year, on the account anniversary.

## 1. Key Findings

1. Under the severe equity scenario (Nifty 50 -20% instantaneous), Kaveri Small Cap Opportunities would lose an estimated 27.9% of NAV, the largest loss of any product.
2. Under the redemption stress (25% of Small Cap AUM redeemed in 10 trading days), the scheme would face a funding shortfall of ₹30.0 crore, which would have to be met by borrowing. This is consistent with the open liquidity breach (11.8% vs 15% floor).

questions.q: What is the cut-off time for getting same-day NAV in Kaveri's mutual-fund schemes?
questions.answer: The cut-off time for same-day NAV in Kaveri's mutual-fund schemes is **3:00 pm on business days** for both equity and debt schemes [1][2]. For purchases, the funds must also be realised in the scheme's bank account before 3:00 pm; otherwise the next business day's NAV applies [1][2].
questions.query: What is the cut-off time for getting same-day NAV in Kaveri's mutual-fund schemes?
sources: Investor Service FAQ – Redemptions, Exit Loads and Statements

cited.title: NAV Computation and Cut-off Timings
cited.text:
## 1. Quick answer: which NAV applies?

For all Kaveri mutual-fund-style schemes (Bluechip, Flexi Cap, Small Cap Opportunities, Short Duration, Arbitrage):

| Transaction | Received by Kaveri before 3:00 pm | Received at or after 3:00 pm |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase / SIP / switch-in | Same day's NAV, **if funds are realised** in the scheme's bank account before 3:00 pm | Next business day's NAV (subject to funds realised) |
| Redemption / switch-out | Same day's NAV | Next business day's NAV |

- **Cut-off time is 3:00 pm** on business days, for both equity and debt schemes.
- For purchases, what matters is when the **money reaches the scheme's account**, not when the investor clicked "invest". A purchase submitted at 11:00 am but with funds credited at 3:20 pm gets the next business day's NAV.
- The time stamp is the one recorded by the registrar's system or the Kaveri website/app server, not the investor's phone clock.
- A "business day" excludes Saturdays, Sundays and stock-exchange or bank holidays in Mumbai.

cited.title: Investor Service FAQ – Redemptions, Exit Loads and Statements
cited.text:
## 1. Buying and redeeming

**What is the cut-off time for same-day NAV?**
3:00 pm on business days, for both equity and debt schemes. Redemptions received before 3:00 pm get that day's NAV. For purchases, the money must also be credited to the scheme's bank account before 3:00 pm; otherwise the next business day's NAV applies.

**I placed a redemption on Saturday. Which NAV will I get?**
The next business day's NAV (normally Monday's).

**How long does a redemption take to reach my bank account?**
Within 3 working days of the redemption date for all schemes. For the Arbitrage and Short Duration funds we usually pay within 2 working days. If we are late beyond the regulatory timeline, we pay interest at 15% per annum for each day of delay.

**Where is my redemption money paid?**
Only to the bank account registered in your folio. We never pay redemption proceeds to a third-party account.

**Can I pay or invest in cash?**
No. Kaveri does not accept cash for any investment, in any amount. Please pay by cheque, NEFT, RTGS, UPI or mandate from a bank account in your own name.

cited.title: KYC and Customer Due Diligence Policy
cited.text:
## 7. Periodic Updation (Re-KYC)

- 7.1 Kaveri shall refresh the KYC of existing clients on the following cycle, measured from the date of the last completed KYC:





| Risk category   | Re-KYC frequency   |
|-----------------|--------------------|
| High            | Every 2 years      |
| Medium          | Every 5 years      |
| Low             | Every 8 years      |

- 7.2 Re-KYC shall also be triggered immediately on: a change in the client's risk category; a sanctions or adverse-media alert; an STR being filed; or a change in beneficial ownership of a non-individual client.
- 7.3 Clients shall be notified 60 days before the re-KYC due date and reminded at 30 and 7 days. If re-KYC is not completed within 90 days after the due date, the folio or PMS account shall be marked "KYC on hold": redemptions continue to be paid to the registered bank account, but fresh subscriptions and SIP instalments are blocked.

cited.title: Distributor (MFD) Empanelment Agreement – Standard Terms
cited.text:
## 3. KYC and AML duties of the Distributor

3.1 The Distributor shall ensure every investor it introduces has completed KYC before the first transaction. Kaveri's KYC Desk performs the CKYC lookup and PAN verification; the Distributor must collect correct documents and must not submit a transaction for an investor whose KYC is incomplete or on hold.

3.2 The Distributor shall support Kaveri's periodic re-KYC cycle: every 2 years for high-risk investors, every 5 years for medium-risk and every 8 years for low-risk investors.

3.3 No cash. The Distributor shall never accept cash from an investor for any Kaveri investment, in any amount, and shall never collect money into its own account. All payments must go directly from the investor's own bank account to the scheme's account. Acceptance of cash is a material breach.

3.4 The Distributor shall tell Kaveri's Principal Officer (the CCO) within 2 working days of noticing any transaction or behaviour that appears suspicious, so that Kaveri can file a Suspicious Transaction Report with FIU-IND within 7 days of suspicion being established. The Distributor shall not tell the investor (no tipping-off).

3.5 Investors who are politically exposed persons (PEPs) must be flagged to Kaveri at the time of the application; Kaveri onboards them only with CCO approval.

cited.title: Politically Exposed Persons Procedure
cited.text:
### 5. Ongoing Monitoring

5.1 PEP clients are permanently in the High-risk category and therefore subject to re-KYC **every 2 years**.

5.2 In addition, the AML Analyst performs an annual PEP review covering: transactions in the year against the stated source of funds; fresh adverse media; and whether the PEP still holds office. The review is signed off by the CCO.

5.3 Any single transaction by a PEP above ₹1 crore generates a mandatory alert, which must be reviewed within 5 working days.

cited.title: Anti-Money Laundering Policy
cited.text:
## 4. Key Controls

- 4.1 No cash. Kaveri does not accept cash in any form for subscriptions, PMS contributions or AIF capital calls. As a result, Kaveri files a "nil" Cash Transaction Report (CTR) confirmation with FIU-IND each month.





- 4.2 Own-account payments only. Money must come from and go back to a bank account in the client's own name. Redemption proceeds are never paid to a third party.
- 4.3 Risk-based approach. Clients are rated Low, Medium or High risk at onboarding. High-risk clients, including all PEPs, undergo Enhanced Due Diligence and are reviewed every 2 years.
- 4.4 Sanctions screening. All clients, beneficial owners and authorised signatories are screened at onboarding and daily against the UN Security Council lists and orders under Section 51A of the UAPA. A confirmed match leads to an immediate freeze and reporting within 24 hours to the authorities named in the UAPA order.
- 4.5 High-risk jurisdictions. Clients resident in jurisdictions on the FATF "call for action" list shall not be onboarded. Clients from jurisdictions under FATF "increased monitoring" require CCO approval.

cited.title: Trade Settlement and Fund Accounting SOP
cited.text:
## 6. NAV sign-off

6.1 The daily NAV is signed off by the Fund Accounting checker, who must confirm all of the following before signing in the fund accounting system:

1. All trades for the day are matched (no open price or quantity breaks).
2. Closing prices are loaded for 100% of equity holdings; any stale price older than 1 day is flagged.
3. Debt prices are the average of the two valuation agencies, or the backup source used after 8:30 pm is recorded.
4. RTA unit capital agrees with the fund accounting unit balance.
5. Expense accrual (TER) for the day is within the approved daily rate.
6. Day-on-day NAV movement is compared with the benchmark; any scheme moving more than 1.5% differently from its benchmark is explained in writing.
- 6.2 On days with a material item (a break over ₹1 lakh, a stale price, or a movement exception) the Fund Accounting Lead gives a second sign-off before publication.
- 6.3 If the NAV has not been signed off by 10:15 pm, the checker must call the Head of Operations.

cited.text:
## 2. Exit loads

**What exit load applies to the equity funds?**

| Scheme | Exit load |
|---|---|
| Kaveri Bluechip Fund | 1% if redeemed within 365 days of allotment |
| Kaveri Flexi Cap Fund | 1% if redeemed within 365 days of allotment |
| Kaveri Small Cap Opportunities | 1% if redeemed within 365 days of allotment |
| Kaveri Short Duration Fund | Nil |
| Kaveri Arbitrage Fund | 0.25% if redeemed within 15 days of allotment |

**Is there an exit load if I redeem my Flexi Cap units after 8 months?**
Yes. Eight months is within 365 days of allotment, so an exit load of 1% applies to those units. Units held for more than 365 days carry no exit load.

**How is the exit load worked out if I invested through a SIP?**
Each SIP instalment is treated separately on a first-in, first-out basis. When you redeem, the oldest units are redeemed first, and only units still within 365 days of their own allotment date carry the 1% load.

**Does a switch between Kaveri funds attract exit load?**
Yes. A switch is treated as a redemption from the first scheme for exit load purposes.

**Are dividend reinvestment units charged exit load?**
No.

**What is the exit load on the PMS?**

| Withdrawal within (from date of each contribution) | Exit load |
|---|---|
| Year 1 | 3% |
| Year 2 | 2% |
| Year 3 | 1% |
| After 3 years | Nil |

**And on the AIF?**
The Kaveri Long-Short AIF III has a 12-month lock-in from each contribution. After the lock-in, an exit load of 1% applies in months 13–24 and nil after that. Redemptions are monthly with 30 days' notice.

questions.q: What fee options can an RM offer a PMS client?
questions.doc: Sales Sheet – Kaveri Focused Equity PMS (for Relationship Managers)
questions.answer:
An RM can offer only two fee options for the Kaveri Focused Equity PMS:

- **Option A – Fixed**: 2.0% p.a. management fee, no performance fee.  
- **Option B – Hybrid**: 1.0% p.a. management fee plus 20% of returns above a 10% p.a. hurdle, subject to a high-water mark.  

RMs may not offer discounts, rebates, or custom fees; any non‑standard fee requires CFO and MD & CEO approval [1][2][3][4][5].

questions.q: What must a relationship manager never promise a PMS client?
questions.doc: Sales Sheet – Kaveri Focused Equity PMS (for Relationship Managers)
questions.answer: A relationship manager must never promise or imply **guaranteed returns, a minimum return, or that the strategy will beat the benchmark**; must never **project past returns into the future** (e.g., “you will double your money in 4 years”); must never **offer a fee discount, cashback, gift or rebate** to win a client; and must never **promise that discretionary clients will get the same returns as the published model** [1][2].

sources: Sales Sheet – Kaveri Focused Equity PMS (for Relationship Managers)

cited.title: Sales Sheet – Kaveri Focused Equity PMS (for Relationship Managers)
cited.text:
## 7. What an RM must never do or promise

- Never promise or imply guaranteed returns, a minimum return, or that the strategy will beat the benchmark. Say "there is no assurance that the objectives will be achieved".
- Never project the past 5-year return into the future ("you will double your money in 4 years").
- Never offer a fee discount, cashback, gift or rebate to win a client. Gifts above ₹3,000 per person per year are not allowed under the Code of Conduct.





- Never accept cash, and never accept a cheque from someone other than the client.
- Never share current holdings beyond the published top 5, or any Investment Committee or research view that is not public.
- Never sign up a client whose risk profile does not match the product.
- Never send this sheet, WhatsApp screenshots of performance, or your own charts to a client; use only Compliance-approved material.

Breaches are treated as mis-selling. Mis-selling complaints are investigated by Compliance, not by Sales.

cited.title: Discretionary vs Non-Discretionary PMS Explainer
cited.text:
### 7. What Relationship Managers must and must not do

- **Must** record the chosen service type in the Client Schedule and in the CRM before activation.
- **Must** explain that non-discretionary does not mean lower risk; the client still bears full market risk.
- **Must not** promise that discretionary clients will get the same returns as the published model.
- **Must not** take trade instructions from a non-discretionary client over WhatsApp or unrecorded phone; only email, the client portal or the recorded line 1800-425-0112 are valid.

cited.text:
## 3. KYC and AML duties of the Distributor

3.1 The Distributor shall ensure every investor it introduces has completed KYC before the first transaction. Kaveri's KYC Desk performs the CKYC lookup and PAN verification; the Distributor must collect correct documents and must not submit a transaction for an investor whose KYC is incomplete or on hold.

3.2 The Distributor shall support Kaveri's periodic re-KYC cycle: every 2 years for high-risk investors, every 5 years for medium-risk and every 8 years for low-risk investors.

3.3 No cash. The Distributor shall never accept cash from an investor for any Kaveri investment, in any amount, and shall never collect money into its own account. All payments must go directly from the investor's own bank account to the scheme's account. Acceptance of cash is a material breach.

3.4 The Distributor shall tell Kaveri's Principal Officer (the CCO) within 2 working days of noticing any transaction or behaviour that appears suspicious, so that Kaveri can file a Suspicious Transaction Report with FIU-IND within 7 days of suspicion being established. The Distributor shall not tell the investor (no tipping-off).

3.5 Investors who are politically exposed persons (PEPs) must be flagged to Kaveri at the time of the application; Kaveri onboards them only with CCO approval.

cited.title: Distributor (MFD) Empanelment Agreement – Standard Terms
cited.text:
## 7. Termination

- 7.1 Either party may end the empanelment without cause by giving 30 days' written notice.
- 7.2 Kaveri may end the empanelment immediately, by written notice, on any of these grounds:
1. Acceptance of cash from an investor, or collection of investor money into the Distributor's own account.
2. Mis-selling established by Compliance, or a promise of guaranteed returns.
3. Lapse or cancellation of the ARN, or action by SEBI or AMFI debarring the Distributor.
4. Submission of forged or incomplete KYC documents.
5. Breach of the no-tipping-off or confidentiality obligations.
6. Sharing commission with investors or with persons without an ARN.
7. Insolvency, or a criminal conviction involving fraud or dishonesty.
8. Any other material breach not cured within 15 days of written notice.
- 7.3 On termination, trail commission stops from the termination date for termination for cause under 7.2. For termination without cause, trail commission continues on existing assets as long as the investor keeps the Distributor as the distributor of record and the ARN remains valid.
- 7.4 The Distributor's investors are informed of the termination and may continue with another distributor or switch to the direct plan.

## 6. Payment Rules

- 6.1 Cash is not accepted for any subscription, PMS contribution or AIF drawdown, in any amount. Branch staff who are offered cash shall decline and record the attempt in the KYC exceptions register.
- 6.2 Subscriptions shall come only from a bank account held in the name of the investor (first holder). Thirdparty payments are refused except for the exemptions permitted for minors (parent/guardian) and employer payroll SIPs, each with a declaration.

cited.text:
## 1. Buying and redeeming

**What is the cut-off time for same-day NAV?**
3:00 pm on business days, for both equity and debt schemes. Redemptions received before 3:00 pm get that day's NAV. For purchases, the money must also be credited to the scheme's bank account before 3:00 pm; otherwise the next business day's NAV applies.

**I placed a redemption on Saturday. Which NAV will I get?**
The next business day's NAV (normally Monday's).

**How long does a redemption take to reach my bank account?**
Within 3 working days of the redemption date for all schemes. For the Arbitrage and Short Duration funds we usually pay within 2 working days. If we are late beyond the regulatory timeline, we pay interest at 15% per annum for each day of delay.

**Where is my redemption money paid?**
Only to the bank account registered in your folio. We never pay redemption proceeds to a third-party account.

**Can I pay or invest in cash?**
No. Kaveri does not accept cash for any investment, in any amount. Please pay by cheque, NEFT, RTGS, UPI or mandate from a bank account in your own name.

cited.title: Distributor (MFD) Empanelment Agreement – Standard Terms
cited.text:
## 2. Commission

- 2.1 Commission is paid only from the regular plan TER and is trail-based only. Kaveri pays no upfront commission of any kind, in cash or kind.
- 2.2 Trail commission is paid monthly, by the 10th of the following month, by bank transfer to the Distributor's registered account, on the average AUM of the Distributor's investors in the month.
- 2.3 Commission is not paid on: direct plan investments; investments made after the Distributor's ARN has

| Scheme                         | Annual trail commission (on regular plan AUM)   |
|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Kaveri Bluechip Fund           | 0.80%                                           |
| Kaveri Flexi Cap Fund          | 0.85%                                           |
| Kaveri Small Cap Opportunities | 0.62%                                           |
| Kaveri Short Duration Fund     | 0.45%                                           |
| Kaveri Arbitrage Fund          | 0.55%                                           |





lapsed; investments made through a transaction later found to breach KYC rules; or units redeemed within 365 days where an exit load applied (commission paid on those units in the first year is recovered).

2.4 The Distributor may not pass on any part of the commission to investors as a rebate, and may not share it with any person who does not hold a valid ARN.

2.5 Rates may be changed by Kaveri with 30 days' written notice. Commission rates are disclosed in investors' consolidated account statements.
